chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ziyad, from Harun ibn Kharijah, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I mix with the Magians, so I eat from their food.' He said, 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat the food of Magians according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Harun ibn Kharijah inquires about the permissibility of consuming food prepared by Magians (Zoroastrians) with whom he maintains social ties. Imam al-Sadiq’s concise reply of 'No' establishes a general prohibition, reflecting the Shia juristic view that their food is not considered ritually pure or validly slaughtered, thereby discouraging close dietary association to preserve religious identity and ritual integrity.
